name: What finishes hold up best in rental units?

mainEntity.name: Which materials are most durable and cost-effective for high-turnover multifamily interiors?
mainEntity.text: Which materials are most durable and cost-effective for high-turnover multifamily interiors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rental finishes should be chosen for durability, repairability, and long-term operating cost. In high-turnover multifamily units, materials need to tolerate cleaning, tenant traffic, and occasional damage without requiring frequent replacement. Hard-wearing flooring, simple trim details, moisture-tolerant bath materials, and easy-to-replace fixtures tend to perform well. In Los Angeles, the right finish level also depends on the target rent band, because spending too much on fragile luxury materials can hurt returns. Owners should prioritize surfaces that look clean and modern but remain practical for repeated tenant use. Good finish choices reduce vacancy downtime and maintenance calls over time.
acceptedAnswer.description: Durable rental finishes usually include LVP or other resilient flooring, washable paint, quartz or solid-surface counters, moisture-resistant bath materials, and commercial-grade fixtures. The best choices balance appearance, maintenance, and replacement cost. Overly delicate luxury finishes often create higher turnover expenses.
